FONE4.why: Down about 59% from the ₹10 issue price (₹4.09) and down more than half in six months (52-week range ₹3.79-11.20). The company is loss-making (P/E negative) and sells phones, laptops, TVs and accessories online. No source gave a company-specific cause for the 2026 slide.
FONE4.outlook: No guidance, analyst view or results commentary found. Market cap is about ₹10-11 crore on 2.495 crore shares.

GSTL.why: Down about 62% from the ₹29 issue price (52-week range ₹5.95-37.65). Revenue fell to ₹16.9 crore in FY25 from ₹25.0 crore and it posted a loss of ₹2.87 crore with operating cash flow of -₹24 crore, per an aggregator. No source attributes the fall to these figures directly.
GSTL.outlook: No analyst forecast, guidance or 2026 results found. It sells cyber security and cloud services. Check exchange filings and any surveillance notices.

FIDEL.why: About 4.9x the ₹37 issue price, but down about 20% over a year and up about 23% over six months (a rebound from a ₹108 low; range up to ₹200+). Weak recent quarters: June 2026 quarter profit down about 47% (₹9.15 crore) with revenue ₹11.56 crore against ₹15.42 crore. ROE is high at about 27%. No catalyst for a re-rating was found.
FIDEL.outlook: Simply Wall St scores future growth 0 out of 6 and its cash-flow model valued the stock near ₹73 against a ₹131.6 price then. No broker target or guidance found. P/E ranges 12-22 by source.

OLATECH.why: Down about 62% over six months from a January 2026 level near ₹212 (52-week range ₹58-291) and about 2x the ₹27 issue price. The sources gave no results or news for the fall. It sells OSS/BSS telecom software, network monitoring, ERP/CRM and cloud services from Navi Mumbai and is listed only on BSE.
OLATECH.outlook: No guidance, forecast or analyst view found. Market cap of about ₹29 crore (28 August) shows how far it has fallen from ₹94 crore in January.

CLOUD.why: Down about 95% from a 2023 peak near ₹191 (market cap then ₹847 crore) to about ₹5.85, below the ₹122 issue price. Possible causes found: a 2023 rights issue priced at ₹123, weak late-2023 results (a ₹2.73 crore loss), and an unverified March 2026 headline about an accounting scandal. Many 2026-labelled pages carry 2025 data.
CLOUD.outlook: No credible forecast or guidance found; FY26 results (year end 31 March 2026) are the near-term test. Simply Wall St scores it 0 of 6 on growth and financial health. Kite had no live quote for it, so the price and market cap are indicative aggregator figures.

CMRSL.why: Down about 61% from the ₹180 issue price (52-week range ₹52-97). It is an ad-tech and data analytics company with TTM revenue of about ₹91 crore and profit of about ₹3 crore (March 2026 quarter revenue ₹17.4 crore and profit ₹1.32 crore). No source explained the price moves; liquidity is low (one day traded 10,400 shares).
CMRSL.outlook: No analyst ratings or guidance found. P/E is only about 5.7 and price-to-book near 1, so the market is valuing it cheaply, likely reflecting the low liquidity and small scale.

PACEECOM.why: Down about 85% from the ₹103 issue price. MarketsMojo (July 2026) cites a 24% year-to-date drop, trading below all major moving averages and delivery volume down 78%. No company-specific cause found. It added software development and IT services to its objects and began IT operations in FY25.
PACEECOM.outlook: No results, guidance or analyst view found. Market cap is about ₹31 crore.

ALLETEC.why: Up modestly on the ₹90 issue price but down about 62% over a year (52-week range ₹115.80-315). Management says growth slowed from longer decision-making cycles tied to global uncertainty and tariff pressure, and from AI-driven shifts; mid-market customers have become cautious. It is a Microsoft business-applications and digital transformation partner.
ALLETEC.outlook: Management expects recovery in one to two quarters, growth in FY27, and a medium-term revenue target of ₹500 crore over four to five years through organic growth and selective acquisitions; growth drivers named are international business, IP-led products, AI, Azure, ERP and CRM. P/E is about 10 (sources range 9.6-28.8).

ANLON.why: About 7.4x the ₹100 issue price, up about 69% in six months. FY26 revenue rose 111% to ₹105.9 crore and profit 114% to ₹13.9 crore, with an order book near ₹110 crore. A ₹22.22 crore five-year operations and maintenance contract at Noida International Airport lifted the shares 9.5% in October 2025, and it started full-scale manufacturing and assembly in FY25.
ANLON.outlook: No guidance or broker targets found. P/E is about 45 (one source 27) on EPS near ₹18.5, so the valuation prices in further growth. The stock is volatile (52-week range ₹335-748).
